issues.legal_issue: A defendant who has been denied a further opportunity to file a written defence and has suffered a decree without contest may be allowed to defend the suit on remand, subject to compensatory costs.
material_facts: The defendants entered appearance in a civil suit but did not file a written statement despite time having been granted.
The trial court declined to grant further time, proceeded on the plaintiff’s evidence, and decreed the suit without a contested trial.
The first appellate court affirmed the decree.
The High Court set aside the judgments and remanded the suit for a fresh trial, allowing the defendants to file a written statement subject to payment of costs to the plaintiff.
The Supreme Court found that the conditional opportunity to defend would do substantial justice to both sides.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right to remand the suit and allow the defendants to file a written statement subject to payment of costs; the appeal against that order was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Procedural rules are intended to facilitate justice, not to punish parties or prevent participation through an overly technical approach. Consistent with the principle of natural justice that a person should not be condemned unheard, procedure should be interpreted with reasonable elasticity where doing so is consistent with justice to both sides. The Court relied on Sangram Singh v. Election Tribunal, Kotah & Anr. (AIR 1955 SC 425).

rule.if: civil_suit_appeal and defendants_denied_further_opportunity and decree_without_contest and remand_allows_defense and remand_requires_compensatory_cost

predicates.civil_suit_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a civil suit.
predicates.defendants_denied_further_opportunity: The defendants were refused further time to file a written defence after failing to file it within the time previously allowed.
predicates.decree_without_contest: The suit was decided and a decree entered without the defendants contesting it on the merits.
predicates.remand_allows_defense: The remand gives the defendants an opportunity to file a written defence and contest the suit on its merits.
predicates.remand_requires_compensatory_cost: The remand makes the defendants’ opportunity to defend conditional on paying costs to compensate the opposing party.

issues.definition: When a civil suit was decreed without contest after the defendants were refused further time to file a defence, a remand allowing them to defend subject to compensatory costs is upheld.
